internal_decisions: Absolute-zero check is done on the input converted to Celsius, compared after rounding to 9 decimals to absorb float error (e.g. -459.67 F).
Regex fullmatch with ASCII flag; leading/trailing whitespace tolerated; optional +/- sign; forms like '12.' and '.5' accepted.

plan: Baseline: tests (19) and acceptance (10) all pass.
Contracts: the two modules are independent, so there is no cross-module boundary to test. Discarded.
Edge cases: tested the absolute-zero boundary in C, F and K, parse variants (+5f, .5K, 12.C, padding), and malformed input (unicode digits, nbsp, exponent, comma). All of these pass.
Low-severity defects D1–D3 are left red on purpose, in qa/test_qa_edges.py.
Integration, regression, non-functional: discarded. The scope is two pure functions, and no code existed before this architecture.
Re-run: python3 -m unittest discover -s qa (expect 3 red tests, D1 to D3).

defects.repro: convert(float('nan'),'C','F') returns nan with no error, because the absolute-zero check is False for NaN.
defects.fix: Reject non-finite values with ValueError in convert, and add that to the section 6 contract.
defects.if_skipped: NaN passes through the library silently, and the caller gets a nan result.

defects.repro: convert(float('inf'),'C','F') returns inf with no error.
defects.fix: Reject non-finite values with ValueError (same fix as D1).
defects.if_skipped: inf is accepted as a temperature, and the caller gets inf back.

defects.repro: parse(None) and parse(12) raise TypeError (from re.fullmatch), not ValueError. Section 6 says ValueError for anything else, and the AC-005 'Must not' clause rules out other exception types.
defects.fix: In parse, raise ValueError when text is not a str.
defects.if_skipped: Callers who catch only ValueError will crash on non-string input.

gaps: Whether NaN/inf should be rejected is not specified in architecture.md, so D1 and D2 are design questions. I did not check bool inputs or very large floats (1e308 overflow).

advisory.problem: The absolute-zero boundary is not tested. No test converts exactly -273.15 C, 0 K or -459.67 F and expects success, and none uses a value just below the limit. An implementation that uses <= instead of < would pass.
advisory.evidence: A convert that raises for temperatures <= -273.15 C passes every test. convert(0,'K','C') is accepted only if the check is done on a differently rounded value.

advisory.problem: AC-005 checks only four inputs. It does not test a unit-only text with spaces, a lower-case invalid unit, or a number with a trailing space and no unit. These are weaker than the brief needs, so they are not blocking.
advisory.evidence: A regex-based parse that accepts '12 ' or 'x12C' as defaults still passes, since neither is tested.
